title: A secret is masked by its shape wherever it sits, and a run record keeps its structure
goal: scrub() masks every secret-shaped value in a text -- a token, Basic credentials, a value a secret word names, a Bearer token, a secret-named environment assignment, a connection string's server, user and password, an address shaped like a user principal name, and a run of 32 or more hexadecimal characters -- and leaves every plain word as written; scrubbed() reaches every string at any depth and redacts whatever sits under a secret-named key, which SECRET_NAME recognises however it is spelled; and scrubRecord() masks exactly the free-text fields FREE_TEXT declares, who was signed in included, and leaves every structural field of a run record, fe_commit first, exactly as it was
reproduce: every failing check names the text, the value or the run record it handed in, which planted secret survived or which structural field changed, and what the contract expects; the probe imports the subject's own scrub module and answers in its own process
